text:
Sen. John Barrasso criticizes Democratic tax plans while announcing rural health funding for Wyoming
Sen.
Sen. John Barrasso, who chairs the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee’s Public Lands, Forests and Mining Subcommittee and resides in Casper with his three children, has used his social media platform to criticize Democratic policies while highlighting investments in Wyoming healthcare.
On October 27, 2026, Barrasso posted: "Democrats' roadmap for a full repeal of the Working Families @TaxCuts:
Dems are radical, extreme, dangerous, and scary."
Later that day, he announced new funding for Wyoming’s rural health sector: "On Friday, @GovernorGordon, WDH Director Stefan Johansson, and I joined healthcare leaders from across the state to announce more than $200 million in Rural Health Transformation Program awards for Wyoming. This historic investment from the Working Families Tax Cuts Act will" (October 27, 2026).
The following day, on October 28, Barrasso continued his critique of liberal policies by stating, "The policies of the liberal left:
Americans demand and deserve better."
Barrasso operates offices throughout Wyoming—including Casper, Cheyenne, Riverton, Rock Springs, Sheridan—and Washington D.C., serving constituents’ needs (official website). He is recognized as a former president of the Wyoming Medical Society and was named Wyoming Physician of the Year. His policy focus includes promoting energy affordability and supporting opportunities for ranchers. Barrasso also emphasizes priorities such as economic growth, public lands management, national parks stewardship, and trade issues.
